description: Service boundary definitions for the Card Transaction Authorisation journey. Documents which service owns which entity and event, what each service's responsibilities are within this journey, and how services interact. Card authorisation is the only journey in the bank's architecture that cannot follow the standard synchronous channel → capability API pattern for cross-capability coordination because the card network latency SLA (<500ms) prohibits synchronous cross-capability calls. SVC-011 makes the authorisation decision locally; all cross-capability consequences are async.
architectural_principles: A service owns its entities exclusively — no shared databases between services
Cross-capability communication is exclusively asynchronous events via SVC-102 (event bus)
Card Processing (SVC-011, CAP-003.05) makes the authorisation decision using LOCAL data only — no synchronous cross-capability calls during the authorisation path
SVC-011 MAY call SVC-009 (Domestic Payments) directly — both are within CAP-003; intra-capability sync calls are permitted
Post-authorisation cross-capability coordination (balance reservation, fraud pattern learning) is exclusively async via EVT-065 and EVT-066
PCI DSS: card_number_token is the only card identifier in all event payloads and entity fields outside the SVC-011 PCI CDE. Raw PAN never exits the PCI CDE.

services.new_service_rationale: SVC-011 is introduced by JRN-011 as the Card Processing Service — the promoted standalone sub-capability of CAP-003. No prior journey has required card scheme connectivity. SVC-011 owns the entire card authorisation and settlement lifecycle: BIN management, card scheme host gateway connectivity (ISO 8583 / ISO 20022), HSM-backed PAN tokenisation vault, authorisation decision engine, local balance cache, fraud rule engine, 3DS ACS, and clearing/settlement processing.
services.pci_scope_note: SVC-011 is the PCI DSS Cardholder Data Environment (CDE) boundary. The HSM-backed tokenisation vault, card scheme host gateway interface, and authorisation decision engine are all within the PCI CDE. All other services in this architecture (SVC-001, SVC-003, SVC-013, etc.) are out of PCI CDE scope.
services.build_vs_buy_note: SVC-011 wraps a card processing platform. Build/buy candidates: GPS (Global Processing Services) or Marqeta as managed card processing platform; or in-house card processing platform with Visa/Mastercard direct scheme connectivity. SVC-011 is the bank's ownership layer regardless of the underlying platform.

consumed_events.name: SuspiciousCardActivityDetected
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-011 PH-044: SVC-011 consumes this event from SVC-013. If recommended_action = block_card, SVC-011 immediately updates the local card status cache entry for card_number_token to suspended_fraud_investigation. This prevents further authorisations on the card until PER-054 (Fraud Analyst) resolves the case. If recommended_action = refer_to_analyst, SVC-011 flags for enhanced monitoring without immediate block.

consumed_apis.call_pattern: Synchronous (direct API — intra-capability permitted; SVC-011 and SVC-009 are both within CAP-003)
consumed_apis.purpose: PH-045 (Clearing & Settlement): SVC-011 calls SVC-009 to initiate BACS/CHAPS settlement funds movement between the bank's settlement account and the card scheme settlement account. This is a batch call — one per end-of-day settlement run. Not in the real-time authorisation path.

consumed_apis.call_pattern: Synchronous bidirectional (ISO 8583 / ISO 20022 authorisation request/response; clearing file ingestion)
consumed_apis.purpose: PH-041/PH-043: Receive authorisation requests and transmit authorisation responses. PH-045: Receive daily clearing files. SVC-011 is a Visa issuer direct participant.

consumed_apis.call_pattern: Synchronous bidirectional (ISO 8583 / ISO 20022 authorisation request/response; clearing file ingestion)
consumed_apis.purpose: PH-041/PH-043: Receive authorisation requests and transmit authorisation responses. PH-045: Receive daily clearing files. SVC-011 is a Mastercard issuer direct participant.
Service account authentication and API gateway authorisation for SVC-011's internal API endpoints. Not in the real-time authorisation request path.

api_endpoints: Internal only — card scheme host gateway interface (ISO 8583 / ISO 20022). Not exposed via API Gateway.
POST /internal/card-authorisations — internal endpoint for scheme host gateway to create CardAuthorisation records (PH-041)
PATCH /card-status/{card_number_token} — internal card block/unblock endpoint (called by SVC-013 consequence of EVT-068 consumption)

local_cache_design.description: SVC-011 maintains a high-performance local authorisation cache (Redis Cluster or equivalent) to support sub-500ms decision making without synchronous cross-capability calls.
cache_entries: card_status_cache: card_number_token → card_status (active|suspended|blocked), updated by SVC-011 on card management events and EVT-068 consumption

balance_cache: account_id → available_balance, card_type (debit|credit), card_number_token. Updated asynchronously: SVC-001 pushes balance updates via internal event; SVC-003 pushes credit balance updates. Cache TTL: 30 seconds with fail-safe policy on staleness.

fraud_rules_cache: Pre-loaded rule set from SVC-013 (velocity limits, MCC restrictions, geographic rules, daily limits). Updated by SVC-013 via scheduled push (every 5 minutes) — not real-time event consumption, to ensure rule cache is always populated.
customer_card_mapping: card_number_token → customer_id, account_id, card_type. Populated from ENT-023 (credit) and ENT-004 (debit) card issuance events.
local_cache_design.cache_staleness_policy: See EX-CA-006 in journey-detail.json. Approve if cached_balance > transaction_amount * 1.10; decline otherwise when cache age > 30 seconds.

services.role_in_journey: Post-authorisation fraud pattern learning and suspicious activity detection. SVC-013 does NOT participate in the real-time authorisation decision path (PH-042) — this is architecturally enforced by the 500ms latency constraint. SVC-013 operates entirely in the post-authorisation async phase (PH-044), consuming CardAuthorisationCompleted (EVT-065) and CardAuthorisationDeclined (EVT-066) to update fraud models and detect patterns across multiple transactions.
services.owned_entities_note: SVC-013 owns no new entities introduced by JRN-011. SVC-013's existing FraudCase (ENT-F001) and FraudEvidence (ENT-F002) entities from JRN-005 are used if EVT-068 triggers a fraud case. The fraud model and velocity counters are SVC-013 internal state — not modelled as journey entities.

consumed_events.name: CardAuthorisationCompleted
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-011 PH-044: Primary input for post-auth fraud pattern learning. SVC-013 updates: (1) transaction velocity counters per card_number_token; (2) cardholder behaviour model with merchant_category_code, amount, channel_country_code, and transaction_type; (3) geographic model with channel_country_code vs cardholder home country. Evaluates cross-transaction fraud patterns. Publishes EVT-068 if suspicious pattern detected.

consumed_events.name: CardAuthorisationDeclined
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-011 PH-044: Decline signal processing. SVC-013 updates decline rate counters per card_number_token. High decline rates on card_not_present transactions signal card testing attacks. Repeated declined auths across different merchants for the same card in a short window trigger EVT-068 publication.

services.latency_note: SVC-013's consumption of EVT-065 and EVT-066 is async — P99 consumption within 5 seconds of event publication is sufficient. The real-time constraint (< 500ms) applies ONLY to the authorisation decision path in PH-042, which SVC-013 does NOT participate in.

services.role_in_journey: Debit card balance reservation and final settlement ledger posting. SVC-001 is a cross-capability consumer of card authorisation events. It does NOT participate in the real-time authorisation decision path. It consumes EVT-065 (CardAuthorisationCompleted) asynchronously to apply a balance reservation on Account.available_balance for debit card transactions, and consumes EVT-067 (CardSettlementProcessed) to post the final ledger debit and release the reservation.
services.owned_entities_note: SVC-001 owns ENT-004 (Account). No new entities introduced by JRN-011 for SVC-001.

consumed_events.name: CardAuthorisationCompleted
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-011 PH-044: If card_type = debit, SVC-001 decrements Account.available_balance by billing_amount_gbp. Creates an internal balance reservation record keyed on auth_id. Idempotent on auth_id. Must process within 2 seconds of event publication (NFR-JRN011-004).

consumed_events.name: CardSettlementProcessed
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-011 PH-045: If card_type = debit, SVC-001 posts the final debit of settlement_amount to Account ledger_balance. Releases the balance reservation created on EVT-065 consumption. Handles settlement_amount ≠ billing_amount_gbp by adjusting available_balance by the difference. Idempotent on settlement_id.

services.role_in_journey: Credit card balance reservation and final settlement ledger posting. Mirrors SVC-001's role but for credit card transactions. SVC-003 consumes EVT-065 to apply a balance reservation on CreditCardAccount.available_balance and EVT-067 to post the final ledger debit. This is the journey that exercises the CreditCardAccount.available_balance cache design decision (DD-ENT023-03) in production.
services.owned_entities_note: SVC-003 owns ENT-023 (CreditCardAccount). No new entities introduced by JRN-011 for SVC-003.

consumed_events.name: CardAuthorisationCompleted
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-011 PH-044: If card_type = credit, SVC-003 decrements CreditCardAccount.available_balance by billing_amount_gbp. Creates an internal balance reservation record keyed on auth_id. Idempotent on auth_id. Must process within 2 seconds of event publication (NFR-JRN011-004).

consumed_events.name: CardSettlementProcessed
consumed_events.purpose: JRN-011 PH-045: If card_type = credit, SVC-003 posts the final debit of settlement_amount to CreditCardAccount statement balance. Releases the balance reservation from EVT-065. Updates CreditCardAccount.available_balance to reflect the final settled amount. Handles gratuity additions (settlement_amount > billing_amount_gbp) by applying the additional debit. Idempotent on settlement_id.

services.role_in_journey: Settlement funds movement. SVC-009 is called synchronously by SVC-011 in PH-045 for BACS/CHAPS payment instructions to move settlement funds between the bank's nostro/settlement account and the card scheme's settlement account. This is an intra-capability synchronous call (both SVC-011 and SVC-009 are within CAP-003) and occurs in the batch clearing phase — well outside the real-time authorisation latency constraint.

api_consumed_by_svc011.call_type: Synchronous intra-capability (CAP-003 → CAP-003 permitted per architectural principles)
api_consumed_by_svc011.purpose: Settlement funds disbursement: SVC-011 instructs SVC-009 to make a BACS or CHAPS payment from the bank's card scheme settlement account to settle the net position with the card scheme. SVC-009 processes the instruction via its existing domestic payment execution capability.

cross_service_interaction_summary.purpose: Card network sends authorisation request to SVC-011 (issuer). SVC-011 responds with approved/declined response code.

cross_service_interaction_summary.timing: PH-041 — published on request receipt, before decision
PH-043 — published after authorisation response sent to card network
cross_service_interaction_summary.routing_note: SVC-001 processes card_type = debit; SVC-003 processes card_type = credit. Both subscribe to topic.

cross_service_interaction_summary.timing: PH-043 — published after decline response sent to card network
PH-044 — async, published within 5 seconds of triggering EVT-065/EVT-066 consumption

cross_service_interaction_summary.purpose: Settlement funds movement via BACS/CHAPS. Intra-capability call (both within CAP-003). Not in real-time authorisation path.
